knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Table 4 and section 5: bromine-treated pools use a pH band of 7.2 and 7.8.
Table 4: bromine at less than 26 degrees needs at least 2.0 mg/L.
Section 6.4: shock dosing is confined to periods when the water is free of swimmers.

practicalCriteria: On a supplied pool, tests bromine and compares it with the minimum for the pool type and temperature.
Identifies from a supplied scenario that BCDMH alkalinity is out of range and states the correction the operator plan requires.
Confirms no bathers are present before a supplied shock dose scenario proceeds.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Bromine test record for the assessed pool
Shock dose record showing the bather-free check
stopWorkCriteria: Bathers present during a planned shock dose: stop, do not dose, clear the pool, escalate.
BCDMH alkalinity outside 150 and 200 mg/L: correct as the plan sets before adding more BCDMH.
Incompatible products found together in storage: stop and make safe.
